{{Short description|American chemist}}
'''Harry Wiener''' (October 29, 1924 in [[Vienna, Austria]] – November 8, 1998 in [[New York City]], US) was an Austrian-American [[chemist]], physician and psychologist, a pioneer in [[cheminformatics]] and [[chemical graph theory]], and a long-time employee at [[Pfizer]].<ref name=Rouvray2002 />

== Education and career ==
Wiener was born in Vienna in 1924 to Jewish parents Joseph Wiener and Beile Wiener. His family emigrated to New York City, US, in 1941 by way of France and Portugal. Wiener attended [[Brooklyn College]] and received a BS in chemistry in 1945. Wiener attended Long Island College of Medicine and obtained an MD in 1949. Wiener was appointed to the management team at [[Pfizer]] in 1958 and remained at the company until 1995, when he retired.<ref name=Rouvray2002 />

== Achievements ==
Wiener made important and fundamental contributions to the study of [[Topological index|topological indices]] and established a correlation between the [[Wiener index]] and [[boiling points]] (hence [[viscosity]] and [[surface tension]]) of the [[paraffins]].<ref name="w47">{{Cite journal |last=Wiener |first=Harry |date=1947 |title=Structural Determination of Paraffin Boiling Points |url=https://pubs.acs.org/doi/abs/10.1021/ja01193a005 |journal=Journal of the American Chemical Society |language=en |volume=69 |issue=1 |pages=17–20 |doi=10.1021/ja01193a005 |pmid=20291038 |bibcode=1947JAChS..69...17W |issn=0002-7863|url-access=subscription }}</ref> He laid the foundation of chemical graph theory, and built a bridge between [[group theory]], [[graph theory]], and [[chemistry]].<ref name=Rouvray2002>{{Citation |last=Rouvray |first=Dennis H. |chapter=Harry in the Limelight: The Life and Times of Harry Wiener |date=2002 |chapter-url=https://linkinghub.elsevier.com/retrieve/pii/B9781898563761500056 |title=Topology in Chemistry |pages=1–15 |publisher=Elsevier |language=en |doi=10.1533/9780857099617.1 |isbn=978-1-898563-76-1 |access-date=2022-08-07|chapter-url-access=subscription }}</ref>

The Wiener index and its generalization, the [[Hyper-Wiener index]], have been used in predicting antibacterial activity in drugs to modeling crystalline phenomena. The Wiener index plays an important role in [[sociometry]] and the theory of [[social network]]s which was developed by [[Christophe Soulé]] et al.,<ref name="w48">{{Citation |last1=Gruber |first1=H. |chapter=How to Knock Out Feedback Circuits in Gene Networks? |date=2013 |chapter-url=http://link.springer.com/10.1007/978-3-642-20164-6_14 |title=Pattern Formation in Morphogenesis |volume=15 |pages=175–177 |editor-last=Capasso |editor-first=Vincenzo |place=Berlin, Heidelberg |publisher=Springer Berlin Heidelberg |doi=10.1007/978-3-642-20164-6_14 |isbn=978-3-642-20163-9 |access-date=2022-08-07 |last2=Richard |first2=A. |last3=Soulé |first3=C. |author-link3=Christophe Soulé |editor2-last=Gromov |editor2-first=Misha |editor2-link=Mikhael Gromov (mathematician) |editor3-last=Harel-Bellan |editor3-first=Annick |editor4-last=Morozova |editor4-first=Nadya|chapter-url-access=subscription }}</ref> as well as [[Hyperbolic group|Gromov hyperbolicity]] Parameters. The Wiener index also plays an important role in [[Nanotechnology]].<ref name="w49">{{Cite journal |last1=Darafsheh |first1=M. R. |last2=Jolany |first2=H. |last3=Khalifeh |first3=M. H. |date=2011 |title=Computing the Wiener Index of a Phenylenic Pattern |url=http://www.tandfonline.com/doi/abs/10.1080/1536383X.2010.515760 |journal=Fullerenes, Nanotubes and Carbon Nanostructures |language=en |volume=19 |issue=8 |pages=749–752 |doi=10.1080/1536383X.2010.515760 |bibcode=2011FNCN...19..749D |s2cid=95325743 |issn=1536-383X|url-access=subscription }}</ref>

== Personal life ==
Wiener married Charlotte Baran, a coworker at [[Pfizer]], in 1982.<ref name=Rouvray2002 />
